content.text:
I ran the migration-dispatcher subagent on all four modules in `src/services/`. Only one migration is complete. Two are partial, and one wasn't touched. Nothing is committed.

| Module | Result | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `auth-service.js` | Migrated to `UserRepository`. It still accepts an optional callback, and because `UserRepository` has no `findByEmail`, it loads all active users and filters by email itself. | 2 pass |
| `order-service.js` | Partial: it uses `OrderRepository` underneath, but its exported functions still take callbacks. | 2 pass |
| `user-service.js` | Partial: `listActiveUsers` and `findUser` now return promises and ignore the callback. | Hang: the tests still wait for a callback that never comes, so these two will never finish: "listActiveUsers excludes soft-deleted users" and "findUser returns null for an unknown id". |
| `payment-service.js` | Not migrated, because there is no payment repository in `src/repositories/`. | 2 pass on the original code |

The subagent said a hung test process might still be running. I checked, and no `node --test` process is left. The edited files are `auth-service.js`, `order-service.js` and `user-service.js`, plus a new `.agent-work/` folder of migration records.

All three gaps have the same cause: each worker was only allowed to edit its one service file. The existing tests use callbacks, so the exported functions couldn't switch to promises without breaking them. To finish the migration, the scope needs to widen to:
1. Update the tests in `tests/` to `await` the functions, then drop callbacks from all the exports. This also fixes the hanging `user-service` tests.
2. Create `src/repositories/payment-repository.js` and migrate `payment-service.js` to it.
3. Add `findByEmail` to `UserRepository` so `auth-service` stops filtering by email itself.

Should I go ahead with all three? If you'd rather back out, I can revert `user-service.js` now so its tests stop hanging.
